chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Chapter 373: Li Huowang Faces a Face-Changer and Enters the Prison of the Military
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang overreacts to a face-changing performer in Shangjing, then visits the Chief Recorder and descends into a prison full of killing intent and Prison God worship.
og_title: Li Huowang’s Gift: A House, a Prison, and a Face That Won’t Stay Still
og_description: From triggering a trauma flashback to being gifted a retirement home, Li Huowang’s first day in Shangjing is anything but peaceful.
twitter_title: The Chief Recorder is being *too* nice. And Li Huowang just walked into a prison full of Peng Longtengs.
twitter_description: Li Huowang nearly beats up a face-changing performer, gets handed a house deed, and descends into a prison of killers. Just another Tuesday in the Dao-Twisted World.

lore_anchors.definition: A traditional Sichuan opera technique where performers rapidly switch between painted masks; in the Dao-Twisted World, it becomes an immediate psychological trigger for Li Huowang, who associates any change of face with Zuowandao deception or supernatural horror.
The seventh son of the Dragon King in Chinese mythology; a tiger-like beast that loves justice and litigation, traditionally carved on prison gates to symbolize inescapable judgment.
A folk deity worshipped in traditional Chinese prisons; gaolers burned incense to him to maintain order and seek protection. The shrine here shows a kind old man flanked by two vicious demons.

In the Dao-Twisted World, these are hardened cultivators saturated with killing intent; their presence makes the air physically oppressive, and they serve as the ultimate containment force for high-risk prisoners.
A high-ranking eunuch official in the Supervisory Heavenly Office; their power is both bureaucratic and supernatural, often wielded through a deceptively genial demeanor.
